question.problem:
Find the least-squares solution to the system of linear equations given below. You're given that the columns of the corresponding coefficient matrix are linearly independent.

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=0 \\ 4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=5 \\ {x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}=-2\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 4 & 1 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5 \\ -2\end{aligned}]}}\end{aligned}
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 4 & 1 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}18 & 0 \\ 0 & 11\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}18 \\ 11\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{198}[\begin{aligned}11 & 0 \\ 0 & 18\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}18 \\ 11\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
